Repeatedly selecting the best validation checkpoint or hyperparameter configuration can overfit the validation sample; the resulting winner’s score is optimistic, even when every training run uses seed 42. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) show selection bias can rival differences between algorithms. Applied here: predeclare the twelve category-condition runs, checkpoint evaluation frequency, stopping rule and tie-breaking; select conditions by the same four-category macro validation HR@10; preserve the host’s held-out evaluation for the final frozen choice. Ablations should change one intended factor while holding splits, candidates, training limits and selection rules constant.

For uncertainty, a suitable conditional analysis is a paired user bootstrap: resample the same user indices for both conditions within each category, calculate category HR@10 differences, then average the four differences equally. Report category effects and the macro difference with intervals. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates; they do not capture training randomness, candidate-sampling variability or adaptive selection bias. [Bouthillier et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098) document distinct contributions from data sampling, initialization and hyperparameter choice. Fixed-seed findings therefore support a controlled comparison at seed 42, without establishing stability across training seeds.

Compute allocation is part of the comparison. [Dodge et al.](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1224/) recommend reporting validation performance against search budget. Here, record every attempted run, failure, diagnostic and checkpoint evaluation against the shared 43,200 GPU-seconds; report per-condition tuning expenditure and best-so-far macro HR@10 versus cumulative GPU-seconds. Four concurrent slots shorten elapsed time without increasing the total GPU-time allowance.
